problem: Saying x̂(t) 'moves one step of Δ volts toward the input' suggests the staircase always closes the gap exactly. If the input is above x̂ by less than Δ, a 1 makes the staircase overshoot the input and the next bit steps it back down. That overshoot-and-return is exactly the granular noise discussed later, so the sentence can mislead a student about how the estimate settles.
fix: x̂(t) always steps in the direction of the input: +Δ when the bit is 1, -Δ when it is 0. If a step passes the input, the next bit reverses it, so the staircase hunts around x(t) with amplitude of order Δ. That hunting is the granular noise of Section 2.
